body:
#!/bin/sh
# pwait.sh — wait on a PRODUCT-run builder (since the 2026-10-19 switch; the prototype's waitm.sh / waitlong.sh stay for
# the fallback). Returns on a dialog (question · permission · plan), a dialog-expired, a session-end, or a turn end at
# which the builder has NO background task of its own (it then waits for the driver); a turn end with tasks still
# running is printed as one progress line and the wait goes on (V103/V105, now from turn-ended's background_tasks count).
#   sh pwait.sh [name] [--after CURSOR]   run in the background with timeout 7200000. CURSOR defaults to the events
#                                          file's size now; pass the size read BEFORE a send so its turn is not missed.
P=$HOME/.local/viola-product/bin/viola
N=viola-builder; CUR=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in --after) CUR="$2"; shift 2 ;; *) N="$1"; shift ;; esac; done
EV="$HOME/.viola/instances/$N/events.ndjson"
[ -n "$CUR" ] || CUR=$(stat -c %s "$EV" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
PIDF="$HOME/dev/projects/additional/viola-overseer/.pwait-$N.pid"
old=$(cat "$PIDF" 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$old" ] && [ "$old" != "$$" ] && kill -0 "$old" 2>/dev/null; then
  for c in $(ps -ef | awk -v p="$old" '$3==p{print $2}'); do kill "$c" 2>/dev/null; done; kill "$old" 2>/dev/null
  echo "[pwait: replaced older waiter pid $old]"
fi
echo $$ > "$PIDF"
progress=0
while :; do
  out=$("$P" wait "$N" --after "$CUR" --timeout-ms 3000000 --json 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then echo "[pwait: wait exited $rc]"; printf '%s\n' "$out"; exit 0; fi
  res=$(printf '%s' "$out" | python3 -c '
import json,sys
d=json.load(sys.stdin).get("ok",{})
if d.get("timed_out"): print("timeout"); sys.exit()
e=d.get("event",{}); k=e.get("kind",""); data=e.get("data") or {}
print(k, d.get("cursor",""), data.get("background_tasks","") if k=="turn-ended" else "")
' 2>/dev/null)
  set -- $res
  kind="${1:-unparsed}"
  case "$kind" in
    timeout) continue ;;
    turn-ended)
      CUR="$2"
      if [ -n "${3:-}" ] && [ "${3:-0}" != "0" ]; then
        progress=$((progress+1)); echo "[progress turn at $(date -u +%FT%TZ), $3 background task(s)]"; continue
      fi ;;
    send-issued|send-confirmed|send-refused|prompt-submitted|activity|session-start|wheel|budget-gate|link|unlink)
      CUR="$2"; continue ;;
  esac
  echo "[pwait: $kind after $progress progress turn(s), cursor ${2:-?}]"
  echo "[host] $(free -g | awk '/^Mem:/{print "mem_free=" $7 "G"}') $(df -h --output=avail $HOME/dev | tail -1 | tr -d ' ' | sed 's/^/dev_free=/')"
  case "$kind" in
    turn-ended) "$P" last "$N" ;;
    question|permission|plan)
      printf '%s' "$out" | python3 -c '
import json,sys
e=json.load(sys.stdin)["ok"]["event"]; d=e.get("data") or {}
print("dialog", d.get("dialog_id"), e.get("kind"))
for i,q in enumerate(d.get("questions") or [],1):
    print("  Q"+str(i)+". "+q.get("question","")+"  ["+q.get("header","")+"]")
    dets=q.get("option_details") or []
    for j,o in enumerate(q.get("options") or []):
        det=dets[j] if j < len(dets) else {}
        lab=o if isinstance(o,str) else o.get("label","")
        print("      - "+lab+" — "+(det.get("description","") if isinstance(det,dict) else ""))
        pv=det.get("preview") if isinstance(det,dict) else None
        if pv: print("        [preview]\n" + "\n".join("        "+l for l in pv.splitlines()))
for k in ("tool_name","tool_input","plan"):
    if k in d: print(k+":", json.dumps(d[k],ensure_ascii=False)[:1500])
' ;;
    *) printf '%s\n' "$out" ;;
  esac
  exit 0
done

body:
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Watch a viola PRODUCT instance and exit only on a state change, so the overseer's LLM wakes only then (replaces the
# 30-minute heartbeat cron: the founder's ruling 2026-11-05, hygiene item 5 (a); measured 2026-10-27, 49 ticks at
# about 1.5 M tokens each). Reads the events file and `viola list --json` only; no model call.
# Exits, printing one line, on the first of:
#   EVENT    — a new event of a state kind: question · dialog-expired · turn-ended (WITH or without background tasks:
#              pwait.sh misses a question asked at a turn end that still holds a task, V150) · wheel · budget-gate ·
#              send-refused · session-start · session-end
#   ROW      — the instance's row in `viola list --json` changed in liveness, wheel, budget_paused or dialog_pending,
#              or the row is gone
# Usage: sh vwatch.sh [name=viola-builder] [--after CURSOR] [--poll S=20]   — run in the background, no timeout of its own.
set -u
NAME="${1:-viola-builder}"; [ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
AFTER=""; POLL=20
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --after) AFTER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --poll) POLL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) echo "vwatch: unknown argument $1"; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
P="$HOME/.local/viola-product/bin/viola"
E="$HOME/.viola/instances/$NAME/events.ndjson"
[ -f "$E" ] || { echo "vwatch: no events file for $NAME"; exit 2; }
[ -n "$AFTER" ] || AFTER=$(stat -c %s "$E")
row() {
  "$P" list --json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c '
import json, sys
name = sys.argv[1]
try:
    items = json.load(sys.stdin)["ok"]["items"]
except Exception:
    print("UNREADABLE"); sys.exit(0)
for i in items:
    if i.get("name") == name:
        print(i.get("liveness"), i.get("wheel"), i.get("budget_paused"), i.get("dialog_pending")); break
else:
    print("GONE")
' "$NAME"
}
BASE=$(row)
echo "vwatch: $NAME from cursor $AFTER · row [$BASE] · poll ${POLL}s"
while :; do
  hit=$(python3 - "$E" "$AFTER" <<'EOF'
import json, sys
kinds = {"question", "dialog-expired", "turn-ended", "wheel", "budget-gate", "send-refused", "session-start", "session-end"}
f = open(sys.argv[1], "rb"); f.seek(int(sys.argv[2]))
for line in f:
    try:
        e = json.loads(line)
    except ValueError:
        continue
    if e.get("kind") in kinds:
        d = e.get("data") or {}
        # The letter's own fixed wait line ("batch X running — this window stays open until its notification") at a
        # turn end with a task is the builder waiting on its own batch, not a stop: skipped (measured 2026-11-05).
        msg = (d.get("last_assistant_message") or "").rstrip(" .\n")
        if e["kind"] == "turn-ended" and msg.endswith("stays open until its notification"):
            continue
        # A turn end with the builder's own tasks still running is a wait, not a stop, unless it asks something: the
        # fix V150 names (a question at a turn end that still holds a task). pwait.sh covers the 0-task turn ends.
        if e["kind"] == "turn-ended" and (d.get("background_tasks") or 0) > 0 and not msg.endswith("?"):
            continue
        extra = ""
        if e["kind"] == "turn-ended":
            extra = f" tasks={d.get('background_tasks')} · " + (d.get("last_assistant_message") or "")[-160:].replace("\n", " ")
        elif e["kind"] in ("wheel", "budget-gate", "send-refused", "session-start"):
            extra = " " + json.dumps(d, ensure_ascii=False)[:160]
        print(f"EVENT {e.get('ts')} {e['kind']}{extra}")
        break
EOF
)
  if [ -n "$hit" ]; then echo "$hit"; echo "cursor now $(stat -c %s "$E")"; exit 0; fi
  now=$(row)
  if [ "$now" != "$BASE" ]; then echo "ROW [$BASE] -> [$now]"; echo "cursor now $(stat -c %s "$E")"; exit 0; fi
  sleep "$POLL"
done

"""Reads class-wall.sh's per-side files and writes class-wall.json."""
import json
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

work, out = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
doc = {}
for side in ("before", "after"):
    code, t0, t1 = (work / f"{side}-times.txt").read_text().split()
    cases = list(ET.parse(work / f"{side}-junit.xml").getroot().iter("testcase"))

body:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The stamped-home class's wall time, before (a scratch clone at the plan's base) and after (the
# tree), each under its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR, the same nextest command over the verify-driven
# override's binary filter. Run from the repository root. Writes class-wall.json beside itself.
set -u
EV=.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-16-wait-wake-condition/evidence
W=target/class-wall
BASE=df3bad61470b
ROOT=$(pwd)
FILTER=$(grep -m1 "^filter = 'binary(channel_endpoint)" .config/nextest.toml | sed "s/^filter = '//; s/'\$//")
NEW="test(=stamped_home_copies_share_no_file_with_the_stamp_or_each_other) | test(=stamped_home_reuses_one_stamp_for_every_home)"
mkdir -p "$W"

if [ ! -d "$W/before-src/.git" ]; then
  git clone -q --shared --no-checkout "$ROOT" "$W/before-src"
  git -C "$W/before-src" checkout -q --detach "$BASE"
  mkdir -p "$W/before-src/target"
  ln -s "$(readlink target/e2e-home)" "$W/before-src/target/e2e-home"
fi
echo "before HEAD $(git -C "$W/before-src" rev-parse HEAD)"

# side <name> <src dir> <filter>
side() {
  local name=$1 src=$2 filter=$3
  local target="$ROOT/$W/$name-target"
  ( cd "$src" && CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$target" cargo nextest run --features fake-agent --profile ci --no-run -E "$filter" ) >"$W/$name-build.log" 2>&1
  echo "$name build exit $?"
  : >"$W/$name-load.txt"
  ( while :; do cut -d' ' -f1 /proc/loadavg >>"$W/$name-load.txt"; sleep 5; done ) &
  local sampler=$!
  local t0 t1
  t0=$(date +%s.%N)
  ( cd "$src" && CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$target" cargo nextest run --features fake-agent --profile ci --no-fail-fast -E "$filter" ) >"$W/$name-run.log" 2>&1
  local code=$?
  t1=$(date +%s.%N)
  cut -d' ' -f1 /proc/loadavg >>"$W/$name-load.txt"
  kill "$sampler"; wait "$sampler" 2>/dev/null
  echo "$name run exit $code wall $t0 $t1"
  echo "$code $t0 $t1" >"$W/$name-times.txt"
  # nextest writes its JUnit under the workspace's own target/, whatever CARGO_TARGET_DIR says.
  cp "$src/target/nextest/ci/junit.xml" "$W/$name-junit.xml"
}

side before "$W/before-src" "$FILTER"
# The two stamp-isolation tests this chunk adds are left out after, so both sides run the same tests.
side after "$ROOT" "($FILTER) - ($NEW)"

python3 "$EV/class-wall-read.py" "$W" "$EV/class-wall.json"

body:
"""Reads class-wall.sh's per-side files and writes class-wall.json."""
import json
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

work, out = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
doc = {}
for side in ("before", "after"):
    code, t0, t1 = (work / f"{side}-times.txt").read_text().split()
    cases = list(ET.parse(work / f"{side}-junit.xml").getroot().iter("testcase"))
    failed = [c.get("name") for c in cases if c.find("failure") is not None or c.find("error") is not None]
    loads = [float(x) for x in (work / f"{side}-load.txt").read_text().split()]
    slowest = max(cases, key=lambda c: float(c.get("time", "0")))
    doc[f"{side}_wall_s"] = round(float(t1) - float(t0), 3)
    doc[f"{side}_max_test_s"] = round(float(slowest.get("time", "0")), 3)
    doc[f"{side}_max_test"] = slowest.get("name")
    doc[f"{side}_load"] = max(loads)
    doc[f"{side}_tests"] = len(cases)
    doc[f"{side}_exit"] = int(code)
    doc[f"{side}_failed"] = failed
    # The split (plan rev 6, step 8): the verify_window_ override (its own 60 s ci kill) and the rest
    # (the verify-driven binaries' 20 s ci kill), and path1_run_start_one_home_in_order's own time.
    window = [c for c in cases if "verify_window_" in c.get("name", "")]
    rest = [c for c in cases if "verify_window_" not in c.get("name", "")]
    rest_slowest = max(rest, key=lambda c: float(c.get("time", "0")))
    path1 = [c for c in cases if c.get("name", "").endswith("path1_run_start_one_home_in_order")]
    doc[f"{side}_window_tests"] = len(window)
    doc[f"{side}_window_max_test_s"] = round(max((float(c.get("time", "0")) for c in window), default=0.0), 3)
    doc[f"{side}_rest_max_test_s"] = round(float(rest_slowest.get("time", "0")), 3)
    doc[f"{side}_rest_max_test"] = rest_slowest.get("name")
    doc[f"{side}_path1_s"] = round(float(path1[0].get("time", "0")), 3) if len(path1) == 1 else None
out.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2) + "\n")
print(json.dumps(doc))

## 2026-11-16-wait-wake-condition — Security Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these): 1 row(s)
**Section:** Security Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these)
**Change:** ~ decision/test-removal-own-dirs-only · state: was «»; now «provisional»
**Why:** decision/test-removal-own-dirs-only: The list's fourth way landed on the delegate's standing direction with the founder away (Q1), so the row stands provisional until his own word.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-16T03-24-03-wrap/

- `wait` wakes only on `turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end`, `dialog-expired` (the one wrapper-appended kind that wakes it, appended through `WaitFeed::appending`); `activity`, `link`, `unlink`, `wheel`, a harness-origin `prompt-submitted` and the send records are log-only. The wake is by event kind alone: every `turn-ended` wakes whatever its `background_tasks`, and telling a finished turn from a paused one is the driver's.

- Test homes on the Linux dev host (the founder's live answer, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, relayed by the overseer; a boundary widening): `target/e2e-home` is a link to the per-user tmpfs directory `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>`, so the fixture chain's sweep and drop and harness `cleanup` create and delete outside the working directory, each only a dir the test side itself made (by its owner record, its own temp dir or its session name prefix) or another build's stamp dir whose lock it takes with try_lock (provisional). The two keepers follow a linked base only when its target is absolute and one `lstat` reads a real directory with no group or other bit, and refuse a backing whose filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), each refusal a fixed message that names no path (the headroom one holds the two counts); they create it 0700 and remove nothing. `viola` never names the backing; no CI runner has the link. Accepted residual (a live round of `viola plugin install`): the round runs the CLI's own four commands (`claude plugin marketplace add` / `install` / `uninstall` / `marketplace remove`) at `--scope local`, a fresh count of four per rig, from a `proj/` that is its own git repo outside this work tree (on the e2e-home tmpfs, no ancestor `CLAUDE.md`): the CLI takes the local scope's project from the git work tree root, and a `proj/` inside the work tree meets the external-imports dialog after the trust dialog; the rig passes the folder-trust dialog by keys into its own pty only, never a desktop key (on a read screen at most 2 arrows toward the trust row and 1 Enter only when that row reads selected, any other screen no key; on a wrapped start the keys move the wheel to the human, and `viola release <name>` precedes the driver's send); the CLI's writes are its own — its trust entry in `~/.claude.json` for each `proj/` whose dialog was accepted, the session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/`, and after the removal its orphaned plugin cache `~/.claude/plugins/cache/viola/viola/<version>/` (re-written in place by a later install and uninstall), `installed_plugins.json` and `known_marketplaces.json` back as before (as measured on claude 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings); viola itself writes nothing under `~/.claude` or into `~/.claude.json`. Accepted residual (a scratch footer reading of a newer CLI): one `viola run` start of the CLI under a tmpfs `--home`, in a detached 80×24 pane, its cwd a fresh `.viola-footer-<pid>/` under the repository root, with no key typed; one `viola list` read against that home; at two instants the pane's bottom three screen rows, scrubbed of the home and the user word, written to the chunk's `evidence/`, never a row above the footer; then the start is killed and its cwd removed; it left no transcript under `~/.claude/projects/` (as measured on 2.1.302 at chunk 2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows). It is no product path and no standing permission: another such reading needs its own answer. A live session's screen frames are kept only under a gitignored local path, never in a work dir, a run dir or a commit; what lands is a closed-word summary per frame.

- **Tempdir convention:** a not-yet-existing home under `target/e2e-home/viola-session-*/home` (harness) or `target/e2e-home/viola-test-*/home` (root rstest chain, `tests/support/home.rs`) — viola creates it, except `tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs`'s `TestHome::outside_scan()` home under the system temp dir, outside G2 / G4 / the secret scan (the founder's ruling, 2026-10-04); kept in CI (`AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`; never under `run --mutants`) until obs gates and the secret scan have read it, a root home's leftover removed only once its recorded owner process is gone (removal deletes `owner.json` last, `remove_owned`; a build's verify stamp dir carries no owner record, and another build's stamp is swept only when its lock is taken without waiting), and on a failing test under `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1` (viola-e2e's booted lifecycle tests through a `Booted` drop guard that stops the session first, and removes the home of a passing test); the base `target/e2e-home` is prepared by a keeper before any home is made (`prepare_home_base` in the root chain, `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home` in the harness), a linked base whose filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`) is refused, and on the Linux dev host it is an operator-set link to an owner-only tmpfs directory under `/tmp`: the path is unchanged, a kept home there does not survive a reboot, and no CI runner has the link

- **Fake agent:** `viola-fake-agent` (root `[[bin]]`, feature `fake-agent`) replays `fixtures/claude/<cli-version>/<Event>.<variant>.json` (the spine, the `<Event>.<stem>-<n>.json` dialog variants and the `paste-<n>` / `compact-<n>` / `clear-<n>` framing variants and the `SessionStart.resume-1.json` resume variant recorded by `viola verify`, the dialog tier by its Runs C and D, the framing tier by Run B's five added pastes, the resume variant by Run E; `2.1.287`'s four relayed dialog fixtures superseded and kept, `RELAYED.md`), runs absolute exec-form hooks from `<plugin-dir>/hooks/hooks.json` (a group's `matcher` evaluated against a tool-bearing payload's `tool_name`), gates script steps on `--control`, and writes an ndjson `--receipt`; its print mode `-p/--print <prompt>` fires the four spine fixtures, prints `ok` and exits 0, `--screens` / `--trusted-root` / `--turn-stop` write `Screen.modal|ready|turn`, `--dialogs` replays a pasted dialog prompt's recorded variants in claim order, and `--framing` replays Run B's recorded paste, `/compact` and `/clear` variants (the probed `/compact` its recorded `SessionStart.compact-1` with the last fired SessionStart's `session_id`) for verify's five interactive runs (two capped test-only holds: `--stop-receipt-hold-ms`, 1 s, holds the Stop receipt for a race test; `--paste-hint-ms`, 10 s, holds a cleared screen after the long paste's turn; and the test-only screen switches `--tag-turn-screen <phase>` and `--long-turn-screen <phase>` draw the named screen after the tag-like paste's turn alone and after the long paste's turn alone) (what `viola verify` drives: `tests/cli_verify.rs` pins verify's lines by literal asserts); CI stamps homes only by running `viola verify` against it at the recorded `DEFAULT_CLI_VERSION` 2.1.287 (the root `stamped_home`, each stamped test home a copy, never a link, of one `viola verify` stamp taken per pair of built binaries, kept under `target/e2e-home` keyed by the binaries' hashes and taken under an exclusive lock, and harness `boot` step 4, unless `--unstamped`; `StampedHome::unstamped` for the unverified-path tests; `SessionOptions::unstamped`, default false, the in-test form of `boot --unstamped` for a harness session); the real `claude` never runs in CI — only the local `run --local-live`, refused under `CI` (`live-in-ci`) — and neither does the real `hyprctl`, which the same fake agent stands in for as `hyprctl` by its own file name in a test-scoped bin dir, reading its mode and reply set from files beside its exe, except in viola-hyprland's own unit tests, which serve `hyprctl` by a planted shell stub because cargo-mutants runs only the mutated package's tests, so a root-package test cannot kill that crate's mutants. The committed `fixtures/claude/*/*.json` (sets `2.1.283`, `2.1.287`, `2.1.288` and `2.1.302`, 12 dialog variants each in 2.1.287, 2.1.288 and 2.1.302, six framing variants, one resume variant and one agents fixture (`Agents.recorded-1.json`, Run B's own row of its one `claude agents --json` read) in each of 2.1.287 and 2.1.302, and 2.1.287's superseded relayed fixtures included; 2.1.287 and 2.1.302 stamped at every relied row, all 24 on every build, 2.1.283 and 2.1.288 drift-only) are walked for hygiene by a run-time directory walk against `schemas/claude-fixture.v1.json`, the `Agents.*.json` agents fixtures against `schemas/claude-agents-fixture.v1.json` (`agents_fixtures_pass_hygiene`), the `Mcp.*.json` MCP exchanges (`Mcp.tools-list-1.json` in 2.1.302, recorded by the test-only `viola-mcp-tap`) left out of that walk and walked by `mcp_fixtures` against `schemas/claude-mcp-fixture.v1.json` (`mcp_fixtures_pass_hygiene`), then replayed against `viola mcp` by `mcp_recorded_exchange` (the served `tools/list` result holding the recorded key and type shape and tool names in order), the `Screen.*.json` screens apart against `schemas/claude-screen.v1.json` (email and row-seam usernames refused too, and a box prompt row with text after the prompt char or a box rule row with any other text: a box row is recorded as its literal alone, `planted_box_row_beyond_its_literal_is_rejected`) (rstest 0.27 `#[files]` refuses an empty glob at compile time); the same walk drives the drift contract `contract_fake_agent_drift`, which compares each print-mode hook's receipt `stdin_hex` byte for byte with the recorded fixture and the hook order with the spine literal, and replays every dialog variant and every framing variant byte for byte, and replays the resume variant (`fake_agent_resume_replay_matches_every_recorded_resume_set`) and, once resumed into its own session, the compact variant (`fake_agent_compact_replay_matches_every_recorded_compact_set`), and compares the key and type shape of the fake agent's `agents` rows with each recorded `Agents.*.json` set (`fake_agent_agents_replay_matches_every_recorded_agents_set`) (the resume launch: under `--resume <id>`, one of thirteen argv options (`--settings <file>` accepted, its value consumed and ignored; beside the options the mode word `agents`, a first word `agents` answering `agents --json` from files beside its exe (`agents-mode`, `agents-rows.json` and the live `sessions/<pid>.json` registry), built on the recorded `Agents.recorded-1.json`, with no option and no env added), the launch SessionStart is the set's recorded `SessionStart.resume-1.json` when the set holds it (2.1.287 and 2.1.302, recorded by Run E since chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows), else its recorded default (a set without the variant, 2.1.288), with `source` `resume` and that `session_id`, or with `--fork-session` the compiled fork id; - **Path 3 — `wait` / `last`** — wakes only on driver-relevant kinds (activity and wheel records, and a harness-origin `prompt-submitted`, never wake a parked `wait`), returns already-logged events at once, typed timeout, exit 21 on a vanished wrapper (`detail` `endpoint-lost` for a wrapper killed under a parked `wait`, after `cleanup` `instance-dead` in a kept home or `unwrapped-name` in a removed one; MCP the same body less `v`, `mcp_tools_a_wrapper_killed_under_a_parked_wait_reads_endpoint_lost`); as landed, the cli + wrapper-channel half (`tests/cli_wait_last.rs`, `tests/chaos_wait_vanish.rs`) in CI on `ubuntu-latest`, the MCP `wait` / `last` steps landed at chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs` `mcp_tools_path2_path3_send_wait_last_match_the_cli`, each result compared with the CLI's `--json` document less `v`); the end-to-end wake witness of all three dialog kinds landed with Path 4 (`question` / `plan` in `path4_dialogs_…`, `permission` in `path4_permission_…`, where a PostToolUse `activity` line wakes no `wait`); a Stop's `turn-ended` data carries `background_tasks`, the Stop array's length or `null`, and an API-error turn end's carries `cause` too, absent on a Stop (`tests/hook_events.rs` `hook_a_recorded_stop_carries_its_background_task_count` over the recorded 2.1.287 `Stop.default.json`, so 0, with `state_events_background_tasks_and_option_details_are_known_keys`; a non-zero and a `null` count unit-tier; live on 2.1.296 on the Linux dev host, a local measurement and no suite, a product `wait --json` woke on `turn-ended` with `background_tasks` 0 and `last` read the turn)
